author: Swinhoe, 1870

art.subject: Mongolian Finch (Bucanetes mongolicus), adult male in spring, a vagrant on a dry rocky hillside in Korea: crown, nape and mantle sandy grey-brown with fine dark streaks; face around the eye and the supercilium washed pink; throat and breast sandy-buff washed rose-pink, the pink extending onto the flanks; belly whitish; wings brown with a pale pinkish-white panel formed by the pale-edged greater coverts and secondaries; tail dark brown with pale feather edges. Bill stout, conical, pale yellowish-horn; eye dark; legs pinkish-brown.
art.pose: feeding on the ground among stones, side view
art.scene: dry, stony coastal hillside with sparse grass in Korea in spring (April), bright light; no people, buildings or text
art.build: A small, compact desert finch about the size of a sparrow, with a large rounded head, short neck and fairly short tail; feeds quietly on the ground among stones. Bill short, deep and conical, pale yellowish-horn, shorter than the head. Legs short, pinkish-brown. Tail fairly short and notched. In flight the pale wing panel and the pinkish wash show; there are no bold wing bars.
avoid: Do not paint a red or scarlet bird like a male Common Rosefinch; the pink is a soft wash on a sandy-brown bird.
Do not paint a dark or blackish bill; it is pale yellowish-horn.
Do not paint bold white wing bars; the pale area is a panel on the greater coverts and secondaries.
Do not paint a long tail (Long-tailed Rosefinch).
